summary: Verdict: monitor (confidence 0.7). F1 confirms delivery of a phishing email from edevlet-burs-basvuru.com with KYK burs subject line (T1566.002). F2 confirms the user clicked the link to the same domain (T1204.001). No new ASN, device, rule, fatigue, bulk-SIS, or token-replay signals survived the follow-up window.

actions.action: Block edevlet-burs-basvuru.com at the email gateway and web proxy; hunt for additional recipients of the same lure.
Reset g.sen@aegean.edu credentials and review recent login/VPN logs for anomalous access.
Issue targeted phishing awareness refresher to the user and similar departments.
Monitor for follow-on payload delivery or credential reuse for 30 days.

limitations: Limited to verified email delivery and click telemetry; full mailbox and endpoint forensics were not performed.
not_checked: Endpoint EDR logs, mailbox inbox rules, and downstream credential use were not checked in this cycle.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1, F2 as unsupported would leave zero surviving signals and the policy would call this benign.

risk.rationale: Verified evidence confirms phishing delivery (F1, T1566.002) and a user click on the malicious domain (F2, T1204.001). This is a real, unexplained suspicious signal, but there is no confirmed credential submission, credential reuse, successful logon, MFA bypass, mail-forwarding rule, or other account-takeover activity to justify "contain." The signals are consistent (no conflict/exposure), so "escalate" is not required, and the click is not explained away, so "benign" does not apply. Appropriate action: monitor the account for follow-on compromise indicators (anomalous logins, password resets, inbox rules, sent mail).
